I’m observing that unlike gravity, objects can only move downward until they hit the floor, with collisions happening when they overlap. The colors preserve the columns while objects stagger based on obstructions along the bottom line. Each object moves straight down as far as it can, colliding with others. I’m figuring out how to simulate this granular physics, considering structures that remain stable under gravity. I'll also calculate final positions for a 10x10 setup.**Analyzing object movement**

I’m thinking about how objects move upward until they hit a boundary or another object. They can only move in a vertical or horizontal domino-like fashion, constrained by their geometry. I have to compute the order of movement in each column, ensuring they align compactly at the top or against other structures. Interestingly, objects can be fixed if blocked, affecting their movement. I should consider how the presence of settled objects influences their upward movement in shared columns.**Validating object positions**

I’m considering how some objects in columns can create bridges with others. When I sort from top to bottom, objects 3 and 4 settle at rows 6 and 7 due to gravity and their initial positions.
